“Find device” has to work while the gateway runs in the background, and Android won\'t let an app ask for that in a dialog — you have to change it yourself: Settings → Permissions → Location → Allow all the time.\n\nSkipping it doesn\'t affect SMS forwarding; it only means you can\'t locate the phone if it goes missing.
This device can\'t open the app settings page. Please change it in Settings by hand.
Gateway commands: status · network · battery · locate · reconnect.\nSend the passphrase followed by the command, e.g. “passphrase status”. The space is optional.

⚠ This phone has a screen lock. After a reboot, Android holds every incoming SMS — and does not start this app — until someone unlocks the phone. The console will show the device as offline.

The good news: unlocking is all it takes. You do not need to open this app; it reconnects by itself about 5 seconds after the unlock, and the held messages follow.

So for truly unattended operation (a power cut while nobody is home), remove the screen lock: Settings › Security › Screen lock › None. Otherwise every reboot needs someone to walk over and unlock the phone once.
Many Android skins block apps from starting after a reboot, and there is no way for an app to check this. Open your phone\'s settings and allow this app to auto-start.
Could not open that page. Go to Settings › Apps › Homing and allow auto-start / background activity.
Settings › Apps › Manage apps › “Background autostart” (top right) › switch Homing on.

Settings › Apps & services › App launch › Homing › turn OFF “Manage automatically”, then switch ON all three: Auto-launch, Secondary launch, Run in background. (EMUI 9/10: Phone Manager › App launch › Manage manually.)
Settings › Apps › App launch › Homing › turn OFF “Manage automatically”, then switch ON all three: Auto-launch, Secondary launch, Run in background.
Phone Manager › Privacy permissions › Startup manager › turn Homing on. Then Settings › Battery › App battery management › Homing › allow background activity.
i Manager › App manager › Permissions › Autostart › turn Homing on. Then Settings › Battery › Background power management › Homing › allow high background usage.

Samsung has no autostart manager — use Background usage limits: Settings › Battery › Background usage limits › Never sleeping apps › + › Homing. Make sure it is not under Sleeping / Deep sleeping apps, and set Settings › Apps › Homing › Battery › Unrestricted.

On Flyme the setting is Background management, not autostart: Phone Manager › Permissions › Background management › Homing › “Allow background running” (not “Smart background”, which still gets killed).
